scenario: Community search over UGC posts, questions, answers and comments. Priorities: nDCG, CTR, semantic matching, query understanding, short-text retrieval, ranking and LLM-assisted search.

papers.title: Learning What to Keep: Transfer-Aware Personal Skill Learning from User Feedback
papers.authors: Li Wang, Chen Zhang, Yirong Yang, Xingyu Chen, Jinkun Zhao, Tianhao Peng, Wenjun Wu
papers.summary: Feedback mixes lasting preferences with one-off corrections. SkillGrain learns which atomic rules to retain and jointly trains skill induction and response generation. On one backbone, it improves the five-task average by 1.61 points over the strongest baseline.
papers.key_insight: Reward rule quality and retention separately. A correct correction can still be unsuitable for future requests; preference stores benefit from explicit scope.

papers.title: Bridging the Topological Divide: Dual-Branch Graph Distillation with Semantic Priors for Robust Cold-Start Recommendation
papers.summary: DualGCN gives interaction-free items a representation through semantic-anchored graph distillation. A separate student learns directions, while inference restores vector magnitude. On Sports cold items, Recall@20 exceeds DropoutNet by 20.8%.
papers.key_insight: Separate direction from magnitude: content predicts an item’s location more readily than its interaction-driven scale. The cold-only evaluation does not establish mixed-catalogue ranking quality.

deep_reading.title: Bridging the Topological Divide: Dual-Branch Graph Distillation with Semantic Priors for Robust Cold-Start Recommendation
deep_reading.content:
DualGCN maps interaction-free items into a collaborative recommendation space through semantic-anchored distillation. It first learns a stable graph teacher, then trains a separate content-only student. The central distinction is between a vector’s direction and its magnitude.

## 1. Problem and motivation

Graph recommenders propagate information through user-item interactions. An unseen item has no edges, so it cannot obtain collaborative information from neighbors. A random ID embedding does not tell the model which established items resemble it.

Titles and categories offer information available at item launch. Yet content embeddings and collaborative embeddings organize items differently: the former reflects semantic similarity, while the latter reflects interaction patterns. A content-only student can struggle to reproduce a teacher whose representation drifts freely under collaborative training. DualGCN therefore changes the teacher as well as the mapping network.

The paper’s strict cold-start setting masks every training interaction for a held-out group of items. This tests representation generation without interaction history rather than adaptation from a few examples.

## 2. Method

### Anchor the teacher in frozen semantics

The model encodes item titles and categories, then compresses those representations with principal component analysis. The resulting semantic features remain frozen. Each teacher item starts from a trainable ID vector plus a scaled, normalized semantic vector; users retain ID embeddings.

Graph propagation supplies collaborative information, and a pairwise ranking loss teaches the teacher to prefer observed items over negatives. The experiments use 64-dimensional representations and three graph layers. Semantic anchors constrain the starting geometry without eliminating collaborative residual learning.

### Train the student separately

The student takes only semantic features. A small network predicts a residual, which is added to the original semantic direction. It does not need to reconstruct the whole representation from scratch.

Training has two stages. First, the student is frozen while the teacher learns ranking. Second, the teacher is frozen and its established-item representations supervise the student. This protects established collaborative representations from alignment gradients.

The student uses cosine distillation, which aligns directions rather than forcing equality in both direction and length. The authors argue that embedding magnitude contains interaction-frequency information unavailable for unseen items. A content-only network should not be required to recover that missing statistic.

![Redrawn framework: a graph teacher learns established items; a content student predicts direction; cold-item inference restores magnitude.](figs/2610.19578/framework.svg)

### Restore magnitude at inference

Unit vectors alone are not directly comparable to teacher vectors in inner-product ranking. DualGCN computes the mean norm of established-item teacher representations. For items below an interaction-degree threshold, it normalizes the student output and multiplies it by that mean. Established items continue to use teacher representations. Both branches are scored against the user’s teacher vector.

This is scale alignment, not a prediction of each new item’s true popularity. The paper defines inference in a shared space, but its main cold-start experiments rank within a cold-only catalogue. That distinction matters when interpreting the evidence.

## 3. Main contribution

The design addresses two different questions: whether the teacher’s space is predictable from content, and which parts of its representation the student should reproduce. Frozen semantic anchors address the first; direction-only distillation addresses the second.

This connects the decisions to avoid end-to-end joint optimization and ordinary mean-squared error. Joint training can entangle ranking and alignment objectives. Squared error also asks the student to reconstruct magnitude, even when its inputs contain no interaction-frequency evidence.

![Original projection: semantic anchors constrain the evolution of collaborative clusters. A two-dimensional projection is a diagnostic, not causal evidence.](figs/2610.19578/collaborative_space.svg)

Ablations support the usefulness of cosine alignment and semantic residuals. They do not establish that magnitude learning is unnecessary in every content-based recommender.

## 4. Experiments

The authors use three Amazon domains. After interaction filtering, they randomly hold out a subset of items and mask all of their training interactions. Established items receive separate training, validation and test splits. Feature-based baselines share the same text features.

The following strict cold-start Recall@20 values come from Table 3. Higher is better.

| Method | Books | Electronics | Sports |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| DropoutNet | 0.0780 | 0.0225 | 0.0926 |
| DeepMusic | 0.0890 | 0.0279 | 0.0827 |
| DualGCN stage 1 | 0.0870 | 0.0206 | 0.0701 |
| DualGCN stage 2 | 0.1007 | 0.0248 | 0.1119 |

On Sports, stage 2 exceeds DropoutNet by 20.8%. On Electronics, DeepMusic still has higher cold-start recall. The evidence supports useful gains across domains, not universal superiority on every metric.

Established-item performance stays close to stage 1 after student training, consistent with the frozen-teacher design. This does not establish unchanged online exposure distributions.

![Original ablation: compare semantic fusion strategies across domains and warm versus cold conditions.](figs/2610.19578/ablation_results.svg)

## 5. Limitations

The authors identify dynamic graphs and richer multimodal signals as future work. The current evidence uses static interaction graphs plus title and category text.

Two additional boundaries affect deployment. First, the cold-start evaluation ranks only cold items. Real feeds usually mix established and new content. Although norm reconstruction defines a shared inference space, the main table does not independently demonstrate exposure allocation or calibration in a mixed catalogue.

Second, randomly hiding interactions after interaction filtering differs from naturally arriving content. Real new posts may have weak titles, missing categories or low-quality metadata. A chronological split would test a different and operationally relevant setting.

## 6. Industrial implications

A platform with item text and an interaction graph could evaluate DualGCN as a new-content retrieval branch. The graph teacher supplies the established collaborative space; the student maps titles, categories or summaries into it. Item vectors can be precomputed, while retrieval retains an inner-product index.

One useful experiment records vector source, norm and interaction degree, then compares exposure and relevance for cold and established candidates in mixed lists. This distinguishes better directional prediction from a score increase caused by magnitude correction.

A second experiment uses actual launch times and reports short-title, missing-metadata and category-specific results. Compare semantic-only retrieval, the residual student and norm reconstruction separately. For UGC search, noisy text may be a more significant constraint than it is in structured product catalogues.

papers.title: Revisiting Generative vs. Dense Retrieval: A Static Value Prior Reverses the Gap
papers.authors: Renbo Tu, Yang Liu, Shuying Sun
papers.summary: A controlled study separates exact-target recall, best-item value and whole-list value. A static value prior reverses generative retrieval’s apparent value lead; on industrial data it improves dense retrieval NDCG@50 by 11.8%.
papers.key_insight: Hold the popularity or value prior constant before attributing gains to personalization. Best-item value and whole-list relevance can favor different retrievers.

papers.title: PersEvalBench: Can LLM Evaluators Judge Contextually Appropriate Use of Persona Information?
papers.authors: Xinyi Liu, Hooshang Nayyeri, Emine Yilmaz, Dilek Hakkani-Tur, Charith Peris, Hari Thadakamalla
papers.summary: PersEvalBench tests whether evaluators can judge the appropriate use of user history through controlled response pairs. On the human-audited subset, the strongest reported judge detects only 63.9% of under-personalization errors.
papers.key_insight: Distinguish omitted preferences from inappropriate reuse. These failures need opposite fixes, so an aggregate satisfaction score hides useful diagnostics.

papers.title: Learning Individual Scientific Taste with Privileged Hindsight Distillation
papers.authors: Hanwei Fan, Yanqiao Wang, Yiqi Zhu, Xuanyu Lei, Peng Li, Yang Liu
papers.summary: The study separates shared, evidence-grounded proposal assessments from individual preference mappings. Hindsight is available only during teacher training. The complete method reaches 0.693 on the reported real-researcher RW-SP metric.
papers.key_insight: Share factual assessment while personalizing trade-offs. Future evidence must remain outside inference inputs; the experiment focuses on research proposals rather than consumer recommendation.

papers.title: xLightGCN: Explainable Graph Neural Network Based Recommendation Systems with Most Influential Peers
papers.summary: xLightGCN decomposes LightGCN-family scores into influential graph peers and quantifies unexplained residuals. Gowalla experiments average each setting over 100 user-item pairs; larger explanation subgraphs cover more of the score.
papers.key_insight: Use the model’s actual computation as explanation evidence. Exact decomposition depends on linear propagation and does not extend directly to arbitrary recommenders.

papers.title: Calibration and Risk-Budgeted Decisions with System One Models
papers.summary: The paper calibrates binary decisions with risk budgets and conservative fallback actions. Across six moderation, safety and reranking datasets, Learn Then Test exceeds the target risk in 7.8% of settings with defined test risk.
papers.key_insight: Fit thresholds to the risk of the action actually taken. Calibration plots alone do not establish that an automated acceptance subset respects its error budget.

papers.title: Similarity-aware generalization framework for zero-shot cross-domain sequential recommendation
papers.summary: SAGERec selectively aligns semantically compatible items and adapts regularization to domain discrepancy for zero-shot cross-domain sequential recommendation. The publisher abstract reports gains but gives no numerical effect sizes.
papers.key_insight: Selective transfer preserves domain distinctions. Evidence is limited to the publisher abstract; the full page returned HTTP 403 and effect sizes could not be checked.
papers.evidence_limit: Publisher abstract only; full page returned 403; online issue date may differ from first-online publication.

papers.title: MgRec: Multi-granularity intent interaction based sequential recommendation method
papers.summary: MgRec combines Transformer-based sequential preferences with coarse-grained intents extracted through a knowledge graph and a neural topic model. The publisher abstract claims stronger recommendations and reduced popularity bias without numerical results.
papers.key_insight: Keep recent behavior and broader intent as distinct signals before fusion. The accessible abstract does not establish the gain over simpler fusion baselines.
papers.evidence_limit: Publisher abstract only; full page returned 403; online issue date may differ from first-online publication.

papers.title: Intern-Decision: Efficient Multimodal Decision Making with Autoregressive Masked Language Modeling
papers.authors: Tong Zhu, Zhe Xu, Zefeng He, Yunkai Chai, Xuyang Hu
papers.summary: Intern-Decision returns structured closed-set choices and candidate probabilities in one causal forward pass. Its 4B model averages 90.02% accuracy across seven evaluation suites. These are decision tasks, not recommendation CTR experiments.
papers.key_insight: A compact choice model can support low-latency auxiliary judgments. Routing confidence still needs task-specific calibration.
